entities.summary:
Geoffrey de Geneville, 1st Baron Geneville, also known as Geoffrey de Joinville and Geoffroi de Joinville, was an Anglo-French noble and supporter of Henry III, who appointed him Baron of Trim, County Meath, and subsequently became a staunch supporter of Edward I. He played a significant role in the Anglo-Norman military campaigns against Ireland and Scotland. Geoffrey de Geneville was a key figure in the Anglo-French nobility, known for his strategic alliances and military prowess.

Born in 1226, he rose to prominence during the reign of Henry III, serving as a trusted advisor and military leader. His appointment as Baron of Trim in 1278 marked a significant milestone in his career, solidifying his position as a powerful Anglo-French noble. Geoffrey de Geneville's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he also played a crucial role in shaping the political landscape of medieval England and Ireland.

Despite his significant contributions to medieval history, Geoffrey de Geneville's life and legacy remain somewhat overshadowed by his contemporaries. However, his influence on the Anglo-French nobility and his role in shaping the course of medieval history cannot be overstated.

The 1314 death of Geoffrey de Geneville marked the end of an era for the Anglo-French nobility, but his impact on the medieval world continues to be felt today.
